source: redactSecretsInRecordedExpectations is a separate, startup-only property from redactSecretsInLog that gates retrieve?type=RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS's own JSON/JAVA/scripting-language/OPENAPI/POSTMAN/BRUNO/HAR forms (src/recorded.rs, src/config.rs). Confirmed against the oracle: PUT /mockserver/configuration echoes the change but has no effect, so this scenario needs its own server, started with it set.

steps.note: default sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie), a default sensitive query parameter (key) and an unconfigured header/query field stay; the body (mentioning 'secret' in plain text) is never touched either — the no-arg FixtureRedactor has no configured body fields, unlike redactSecretsInLog's fixtureBodyRedactFields

RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS JSON: request headers/query and the response Set-Cookie header redacted; a parsed cookies field (request and response) stays unredacted even though the Cookie/Set-Cookie header carrying the same value is masked (verified against the oracle); id/times/timeToLive preserved (8.0.0; adopted upstream c76143e4a masks the parsed cookies too: diverge)
RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS JAVA (input form): the same redaction
RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS JAVASCRIPT (a scripting-language export, from the same redacted canonical list as JSON)
RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS HAR: redacted like POSTMAN/BRUNO/OPENAPI (all built from recorded_input/recorded)
RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS CURL: unaffected either way, always 'not supported'
RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS LOG_ENTRIES: NOT gated by this property (verified against the oracle) — the raw Authorization/Cookie/key values are expected in this golden
